t: A federation of Greek cities with shared citizenship, coinage and foreign policy, led by an annually elected general.
Under Aratus and Philopoemen it grew from four Achaean towns to the whole Peloponnese by 191 BCE.
Rome dissolved it after the war of 146 BCE and the sack of Corinth; Polybius made it a model for later federal thinkers.
dyk: James Madison discussed the Achaean League in The Federalist No. 18 as a lesson for the new United States on the strengths and dangers of federal union.
ev: Dyme, Patrae, Tritaia and Pharai renew the Achaean League
Aratus frees Sicyon and brings it into the league
Aratus seizes Acrocorinth from the Macedonians
The league cedes Acrocorinth to Antigonus III Doson for help against Sparta
Philopoemen defeats Machanidas of Sparta at Mantinea
With Messene and Elis, the league unites the whole Peloponnese
About 1,000 Achaeans, including Polybius, are deported to Italy
Rome defeats the league and Lucius Mummius sacks Corinth

f.capital: Aigion (federal sanctuary of Zeus Homarios); later meetings rotated among member cities
f.successor: Roman Republic (later the province of Achaea)
